answer: Sybil resistance here is a compounding lock-and-percolation rule. Each new identity must park a non-transferable bond in a time-locked oasis, and every extra key the same operator opens lengthens that unlock. Voting and mining rights do not start at deposit; they only percolate after the bond has seeped through a karst of independent graders whose sealed scores must agree the operator produced original work. Until that path opens, the identity is inert in the wider ocean of settlement, so a swarm pays stacked lockup without buying influence.
